newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, bull trend seen next week.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, bull trend seen next week.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Friday with drugs concern Pliva trading heavily after hitting an all-time high on the back of the strong dollar and traders predicted the bullish trend would continue next week.
"I expect a short-term bullish trend next week and then, if investors have bought enough, there will be a lull in August," said Domagoj Grabovac of FIMA brokerage.
Seven of 17 active issues rose on Friday, six fell, three were flat and one traded for the first time. Volume rose to 19,863 units and turnover to 12.3 million kuna.
Pliva and the other fully-listed stock Zagrebacka Banka both hit record highs, in line with the rise of their Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in London.

"Since Pliva's record highs in London in January, the dollar has risen at least 12 percent. The records on Croatian bourse are still 10 percent lower, so there is room for further growth of both Pliva and Zagrebacka," Grabovac said.
Pliva was the day's biggest gainer, adding 24 kuna or 4.5 percent to 560. It was also the most active issue with 9,543 shares sold.
Zagrebacka's ordinaries added 44.88 kuna to 2,350, with 1,958 shares sold.

The upward trend is obviously continuing and it encouraged foreign investors to get involved in livelier trading. That also positively affected other leading stocks like (food concern) Podravka, Grabovac said.
Podravka added eight kuna to 260 with 2,058 units sold.
Croatia's leading confectioner Kras added three kuna to 410 on modest volume of 277 units, but Grabovac warned the stock rose "unrealistically", boosted by good trading of other blue chips.
Fully-listed Varazdinska banka's 1-series was flat at 210 kuna with 2,072 shares sold.
Its 2-series, mostly owned by small share-holders was Friday's biggest decliner, losing 70 kuna or 40 percent to 105, with 25 units sold. The stock last traded on June 20.
The favouring of blue chips had a negative impact on other stocks like brewery Karlovacka Pivovara and hotelier Laguna Porec.
"They are in an unfavourable position now, because everything is in the shadow of the blue chips," Graboca said.
Karlovacka lost 15 kuna to 550, with only 75 shares sold.
Laguna eased three kuna to 1,432, selling 180 units.
The only other active hotelier, Rivijera Porec, lost one kuna to 157, with 48 shares changing hands.
